transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that I’ve... I've sort of gotten stuck doing these little routines lately. It's mostly things like washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace, or going back to recheck the stove and the front door. I also find myself silently counting through steps before I leave the house. 

It's frustrating because they’re starting to make me late for things, even when I know perfectly well that I’ve already done enough. I just thought it was time to come in and get some advice on it.
Do you have any disturbing or intrusive thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?

Yes, I do. I’ll just be sitting at home reading, or getting ready for my shift at the museum, and... well, an ugly little thought just keeps barging in. It's usually a worry that I’ve left something unsafe, or maybe touched something unclean. Or that I've somehow put someone at risk. It's frustrating because I know perfectly well it’s out of proportion, but the thought just keeps repeating anyway.
Do you feel like you have to perform these routines to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes, that is exactly it. Like I was saying earlier about getting stuck in those routines... I do them because it feels like if I don't, one of those worries will actually come true. 

If I don't wash my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or if I don't go back to check the stove and the front door, I just can't shake the feeling that a fire might start or someone might get sick. Doing the counting and the checking... it's like I have to do it to prevent the bad thing from happening. It's the only way to quiet the thought down, even though, like I said, it ends up making me late and I know perfectly well I've already done enough.
Do you have any compulsions to perform physical actions, like washing or checking, in response to your intrusive thoughts?

Yes, that's exactly it. I think that goes back to what I was mentioning when we first started talking, since that's really the main reason I made this appointment. 

I get stuck doing those physical routines—like washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace, or physically walking back to recheck the stove and the front door. And then there's the silent counting I do before I leave the house. I do all of those actions in response to those thoughts, and it's just frustrating. Like I said, they’re starting to make me late for things, even when I know perfectly well that I’ve already done enough.

Are your routines, like washing your hands or checking the stove, specifically intended to prevent a particular bad event from happening, or are they more about making you feel less anxious or uncomfortable?

I suppose it's a bit of both. Like I've been mentioning, what really brought me in to see you today is that I’ve gotten so stuck doing these little routines. The washing my hands again after handling my wrist brace, the rechecking the stove and the front door, the silently counting through my steps before I leave... 

I do them because my mind is telling me it will prevent something bad, but completing the action is also the only thing that relieves that uncomfortable, anxious feeling. If I don't do the routine, the worry just sits there. The problem is just that I get stuck, and repeating these steps is starting to make me late for things, even when I know perfectly well I’ve already done enough.
Are the bad things you're trying to prevent with your routines, like fires or someone getting sick, always the same or do they vary?

Well, I guess... I'm not really sure if they vary or not. I haven't paid that much attention to it. I just know that the thoughts pop up, and then I feel like I have to do the checking or the washing to make them stop. I haven't really tracked if it's always the exact same bad thing I'm worried about every single time.
Are your worries and the bad things you're trying to prevent always related to one specific type of threat, like safety or contamination?

Well, no, it's not really limited to just one specific type of threat. It's a mix of those things. I’ll just be sitting and reading at home, or maybe getting ready for my shift at the museum, and... well, an ugly little thought just keeps barging in. 

Sometimes it's a worry that I’ve left something unsafe, like the stove or the door. Other times it's that I've touched something unclean. Or even just a general fear that I've somehow put someone at risk. So it jumps around between safety and contamination, even though I know perfectly well that the worry is completely out of proportion.
Do you feel like you have to perform your routines in a specific or 'just right' way?

Yes, I do. Like I mentioned a few minutes ago about why I came in... getting stuck in those routines. When I wash my hands after handling my wrist brace, or when I'm rechecking the stove and the front door, it's not just a quick glance. I have to do it a certain way. 

That's why I do that silent counting through my steps before I leave the house. If the count gets messed up, or if the action just doesn't feel... settled, I guess, I have to do it again until it feels correct. That's exactly how I end up getting stuck and running late, because I keep repeating it to get it right, even when I know perfectly well I’ve already done enough.
Do you feel like your daily activities or routines need to be symmetrical or perfectly balanced in some way?

No, I don't really have that issue. It's more about the counting and making sure things feel settled, like I was saying, rather than needing things to be perfectly symmetrical or balanced. I don't really pay attention to how things are lined up or anything like that.
Do you ever feel the need to repeat certain words or phrases to yourself as a way to cope with your intrusive thoughts?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I do that silent counting I told you about when I'm checking the door or the stove, but... no, as far as actually repeating specific words or phrases to myself, I haven't noticed doing anything like that. It's really just the numbers for me.
Do you feel like the counting you do is aimed at preventing something bad from happening or is it more about reaching a specific number that feels right to you?

I think it's more about reaching a number that feels right. Like I was saying earlier about what brought me in... the main issue is just getting stuck doing these little routines. 

When I wash my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or when I'm rechecking the stove and the front door, that silent counting through my steps isn't really to prevent a fire or a break-in. It's just that the count has to feel right and settled. If it doesn't, I have to start over. And that's the whole problem—I get stuck repeating the routine until the count feels correct, and it ends up making me late, even though I know perfectly well I've already done enough.
Do you feel like your compulsions, such as the counting, are driven by a need to make things feel exact or just right?

Yes, I think that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, it really comes down to that feeling of it being just right. I don't know if I'd use the word exact, necessarily, but the count just has to feel settled in my mind before I can move on. If it doesn't feel right, I just can't walk away from the door or the stove.
Do you feel like these compulsions to perform routines, such as counting or checking, are in line with your own desires and values, or do they feel foreign or contradictory to who you are?

I don't really know if I'd use those words. I haven't thought about it in terms of my values or... or it being foreign to who I am, exactly. 

I mean, I definitely don't want to be doing it, mostly just because it's a nuisance and it ends up making me late for things. But I wouldn't say it feels contradictory to my identity or anything like that. It's really just... well, it's just this frustrating habit I get stuck in.
Do you feel like these habits are significantly interfering with your daily life or causing you a lot of distress?

Well, I’m still managing on my own, so I wouldn't say it's causing me severe distress. But it definitely interferes. 

Like I mentioned, it makes me late. I volunteer as a docent, and these routines have made me late to my shifts. I've actually even skipped a few museum events lately because... well, just the whole process of getting out the door feels like too much. It just becomes such a hassle to get through the checking and the counting that sometimes it's easier just to stay home.
Do you find that the same intrusive thoughts keep repeating over time?

Yes, they definitely repeat. It's usually the same kind of thing over and over. I'll just be sitting at home reading, or maybe getting ready for one of my museum shifts, and this... this ugly little thought just barges in. 

It's always something like I've left a situation unsafe, or maybe I touched something unclean, or that I've somehow put someone at risk. And the frustrating part is, I know perfectly well that it's blown out of proportion. But the thought just keeps coming back anyway.
Are your compulsions, such as washing or checking, primarily done to prevent a specific bad event from happening or to reduce your overall feeling of anxiety?

Well, it's really to prevent a bad event, I suppose. That's actually what brings me in... I've just gotten stuck doing these little routines. Like, I'll wash my hands again after handling my wrist brace, or I'll recheck the stove and the front door. Sometimes I silently count through steps before I leave the house. 

I do them because I feel like I have to, to make sure nothing bad happens. But it's just... they're starting to make me late for things, even when I know perfectly well I've already done enough. It's just to get rid of that feeling that something is going to go wrong.
Are your compulsions, such as checking the stove or washing your hands, more about preventing harm to yourself or to others?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought about it quite like that. 

It's just... a general fear of a disaster. Like with the stove, I suppose that would hurt me if there was a fire, but it could spread to the neighbors, too. And the washing... I just don't want sickness spreading, to me or anyone else. 

So, I don't really know if it's strictly one or the other. I haven't noticed it being specific to just me or just other people. It's really just about making sure nothing terrible happens in general.
Is your need to wash your hands after handling your wrist brace more about preventing the spread of illness or something else?

I'm not exactly sure, to tell you the truth. I haven't really pinned down a specific reason like that. 

With the wrist brace, I don't know if I'm necessarily picturing catching a specific illness... it's more just a general feeling that my hands are unclean after I take it off or adjust it. I just know that if I don't wash them right then, I can't shake the feeling that something is wrong. So I guess I don't really have a clear answer for what exactly I'm trying to prevent in that specific instance.
Is the thought of contamination the primary driver for your need to wash your hands after handling your wrist brace?

I suppose it is, yes. The feeling of touching something unclean is definitely a big part of it. 

It's... well, it's like I'll just be reading at home, or getting ready for my shift at the museum, and this ugly little thought keeps barging in. It just tells me that I've touched something unclean, like the brace, or maybe that I've left something unsafe and somehow put someone at risk. I know perfectly well that it's completely out of proportion, but the thought just pushes its way in anyway.
Do you think your intrusive thoughts or the actions you feel compelled to take are more distressing to you?

I'm... not entirely sure how to separate the two, really. I haven't really thought about which one is worse. 

The thoughts are upsetting because they just pop up and won't leave me alone, but then doing the washing or the checking... that's frustrating too, because I know I don't need to do it, but I feel like I have to. 

So, I don't know if one is more distressing than the other. They kind of just go hand in hand for me.

The symptom profile for compulsions (S066) mentions washing hands after handling the wrist brace, but it does not specify the exact underlying fear or motivation for this specific action beyond what has already been discussed in previous turns.

patient.answer:
I'm not exactly sure, to tell you the truth. I haven't really pinned down a specific reason like that. 

With the wrist brace, I don't know if I'm necessarily picturing catching a specific illness... it's more just a general feeling that my hands are unclean after I take it off or adjust it. I just know that if I don't wash them right then, I can't shake the feeling that something is wrong. So I guess I don't really have a clear answer for what exactly I'm trying to prevent in that specific instance.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's compulsions are driven by a fear of contamination or harm
doctor.question: Is the thought of contamination the primary driver for your need to wash your hands after handling your wrist brace?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: I’ll be reading at home or getting ready for a museum shift, and an ugly little thought keeps barging in that I’ve left something unsafe, touched something unclean, or somehow put someone at risk, even though I know perfectly well it’s out of proportion.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is asking about the 'thought of contamination' which refers to the intrusive, unwanted thoughts (obsessions) that drive the compulsion to wash hands.

patient.answer:
I suppose it is, yes. The feeling of touching something unclean is definitely a big part of it. 

It's... well, it's like I'll just be reading at home, or getting ready for my shift at the museum, and this ugly little thought keeps barging in. It just tells me that I've touched something unclean, like the brace, or maybe that I've left something unsafe and somehow put someone at risk. I know perfectly well that it's completely out of proportion, but the thought just pushes its way in anyway.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are more aligned with obsessive-compulsive disorder with predominantly obsessive symptoms or with compulsive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you think your intrusive thoughts or the actions you feel compelled to take are more distressing to you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking the patient to compare the distress levels between their obsessions (intrusive thoughts) and compulsions (actions). The symptom profiles detail the presence and manifestations of obsessions and compulsions, but do not contain a specific comparison of which is more distressing to the patient.

patient.answer:
I'm... not entirely sure how to separate the two, really. I haven't really thought about which one is worse. 

The thoughts are upsetting because they just pop up and won't leave me alone, but then doing the washing or the checking... that's frustrating too, because I know I don't need to do it, but I feel like I have to. 

So, I don't know if one is more distressing than the other. They kind of just go hand in hand for me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of repetitive behaviors (e.g., washing hands, checking stove and front door) and mental acts (e.g., silent counting) aimed at preventing or reducing distress or preventing some dreaded event or situation, align with the diagnostic criteria for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD). The presence of intrusive thoughts and compulsions to perform specific rituals to alleviate anxiety support this diagnosis.
